knowledgePattern: Factor a recurrence and shift its terms to expose a convergent GP

hints.title: Factor the recurrence
hints.body: Factor its right-hand side and compare the factor with the multiplier on the left.
hints.recap: A common factor may be cancelled only when it is nonzero.
hints.pitfall: Check separately whether a forbidden cancellation value can ever be reached by this sequence.
hints.pause: Simplify the recurrence on its valid domain.

recall.reminder: A common factor may be cancelled only when it is nonzero.

hints.title: Follow the terms that are actually summed
hints.body: Write a recurrence for bn=an+1 rather than trying to sum an directly.
hints.recap: The sequence being summed may differ from the sequence used to state a recurrence.
hints.pitfall: Carry the added constant through both sides of the recurrence.
hints.pause: Identify the new first term and ratio, verify convergence and calculate the infinite sum.

recall.reminder: The sequence being summed may differ from the sequence used to state a recurrence.

solution:
1. The recurrence factors as an+1(an−1)=12(an−1)2. Whenever an≠1, it gives an+1=(an−1)/2.

2. Cancellation is safe for this sequence: a1=2 gives a2=1/2; thereafter any term less than 1 produces a negative next term, which is again less than 1. Thus the cancelled factor never vanishes.

3. Let bn=an+1, the quantity being summed. Then bn+1=12(an−1)+1=12bn, and b1=3.

4. This GP has ratio 1/2, so its sum to infinity is 3/(1−1/2)=6. Answer D. The terms an themselves approach −1; it is the shifted terms that are summed.
